note.title: Mixed exam practice
note.overview: A 60-mark mixed assessment combines recall, calculation, practical planning and linked explanations across the Year 8 course.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 vocabulary for mixed exam practice.
Apply the knowledge rather than relying on recognition alone.
Use the command word and include every required scientific point.
mustMemoriseRules: Read the command word and mark allocation.
One clear scientific point normally earns one mark.
Calculations need working and units; long answers need linked causal steps.

workedExamples.answer: Write six linked stages from variation to allele-frequency change.
workedExamples.why: Explain biological ideas as linked steps: name the structure or process, state what happens, and connect it to the effect on the cell, organism or ecosystem. Use precise scientific terms rather than everyday substitutes.

commonMistakes: Writing more without adding mark points.
Missing a subpart of a multi-part question.
Using vague words where a precise term is required.
detailedExplanation: A 60-mark mixed assessment combines recall, calculation, practical planning and linked explanations across the Year 8 course.

Explain biological ideas as linked steps: name the structure or process, state what happens, and connect it to the effect on the cell, organism or ecosystem. Use precise scientific terms rather than everyday substitutes.
examTips: Plan long answers as one point per available mark.
Check every requested element before submitting.
Use the command word and number of marks to decide how many distinct points are required.
Use precise terminology and link cause to effect rather than listing disconnected facts.
For calculations, show the relationship, substitution, working and unit.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key terms once, then cover them.
Say or write the answer before using MC recognition.
For exam questions, count the marks and check each point.
